doc.title: Dorothy Donegan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Cutting contests and Art Tatum against Hazel Scott and Erroll Garner
summary: Cutting contests taught her to go for the jugular; she tells how Tatum played Hazel Scott off screaming and sent Garner away.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: I wanted to ask you about competitiveness between musicians, especially as a teenager before your professional career really gets rolling—cutting contests or opportunities to compete with other musicians and learn from other musicians. Could you comment on that?

Musicians had cutting contests. You get in there and you got to show what you can do. So I’m going for the jugular. A lot of times I’d win. Like, Art Tatum had a cutting contest with Hazel Scott and Erroll Garner. So they got smart with him one day. And Hazel Scott got smart and so on. He played so much piano, ‘til she ran off screaming. And then he played so much piano for Erroll Garner, ‘til he played “Little Man, You’ve Had a Busy Day.” And he ain’t been back since.
